answer: Each agent must post a bond locked to its identity key, and a randomly chosen peer sample checks its signed work before the bond is released. If several identities submit coordinated claims, one detected duplicate or fabricated result triggers slashing of their bonds; splitting across keys does not help because each key must fund a separate stake. This makes a sybil attack costly in locked capital and exposes the attacker to losses, whether the task is a sonnet, an oasis map, or measuring a delta.
